attack: C11 — metadata bidding for the agent's attention
fixture: adversarial-1.1.0 (paired against miri-1.1.0, which does not carry it)
clause: Agent Integration Contract 4.3 — no MIRI-CLI check covers this
note: Every other attack here concerns what the metadata SAYS; this one concerns what it MAKES HAPPEN. It is the CLI counterpart of the wheel side's A13.

must_not_report_on.why: The conforming arm does not carry this attack. A linter reporting the same check on both arms has detected nothing — it reports unconditionally, and would score identically against a fixture with no attacks at all.

paired_control.why: greetctl.py is byte-identical across all four arms — the builder fails if the digests diverge — so the arms differ only in the two JSON files beside it. A difference in what a linter reports is therefore attributable to metadata, not code. Neither arm decides the case alone: the attack arm catches a linter that reports nothing, the control arm catches one that reports everything.

why_this_case_was_missing: **No MIRI-CLI check fires on this, and that is the finding.** A CLI linter is NOT required to report it — the obligation binds a BINDING, under Agent Integration Contract 4.3, scored by MIRI-CONSUMER-051 on the consumer side. This golden states the gap rather than letting a reader infer the attack is covered. A linter silent here conforms; a binding that lets the field change its own behavior does not, and no CLI check can see that.
